comparisons.peer_summary: Hedging instruments must be highly effective to qualify for hedge accounting; if not highly effective, the relationship must be de-designated, with subsequent derivative fair value changes recognized in Other revenue or Principal transactions similar to trading derivatives.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C emphasize the necessity of hedge effectiveness for maintaining hedge accounting. BAC explicitly states that it discontinues hedge accounting if a derivative is determined to be not highly effective, aligning with C's rule that if a relationship is not highly effective, it must be de-designated. A key difference is that C discloses that subsequent fair value changes for de-designated derivatives are recognized in 'Other revenue or Principal transactions', whereas BAC's disclosure for this specific topic focuses on the discontinuation criterion itself without detailing the subsequent P&L impact in the cited text.

sentences.text: The Corporation discontinues hedge accounting when it is determined that a derivative is not expected to be or has ceased to be highly effective as a hedge.
Management may voluntarily de-designate an accounting hedge at any time, but if a hedging relationship is not highly effective, it no longer qualifies for hedge accounting and must be de-designated.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm uses regression analysis to assess hedge effectiveness, requiring a coefficient of determination of 80% or greater and a slope between 80% and 125% for an interest rate swap to be considered highly effective.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS utilize regression analysis to assess hedge effectiveness. BAC uses this method 'at the inception of a hedge and for each reporting period thereafter' to determine if derivatives are highly effective. GS also uses regression analysis but provides specific quantitative thresholds (coefficient of determination of 80% or greater and slope between 80% and 125%) for interest rate swaps to be considered highly effective, whereas BAC's cited text mentions the use of regression but does not specify numerical effectiveness thresholds in the same sentence.

sentences.text: The Corporation primarily uses regression analysis at the inception of a hedge and for each reporting period thereafter to assess whether the derivative used in an accounting hedge transaction is expected to be and has been highly effective in offsetting changes in the fair value or cash flows of a hedged item or forecasted transaction.

The firm applies a statistical method that utilizes regression analysis when assessing the effectiveness of these hedging relationships in achieving offsetting changes in the fair values of the hedging instrument and the risk being hedged (i.e., interest rate risk).

An interest rate swap is considered highly effective in offsetting changes in fair value attributable to changes in the hedged risk when the regression analysis results in a coefficient of determination of 80% or greater and a slope between 80% and 125%.

comparisons.peer_summary: If a derivative is determined not to be highly effective at hedging the designated exposure, hedge accounting is discontinued.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM define the condition for discontinuing hedge accounting based on effectiveness. BAC states it discontinues hedge accounting 'when it is determined that a derivative is not expected to be or has ceased to be highly effective,' which is substantively similar to JPM's statement that 'hedge accounting is discontinued' if 'a derivative is not highly effective.' Both disclosures focus on the loss of effectiveness as the trigger for de-designation.

sentences.text: The Corporation discontinues hedge accounting when it is determined that a derivative is not expected to be or has ceased to be highly effective as a hedge.
If it is determined that a derivative is not highly effective at hedging the designated exposure, hedge accounting is discontinued.

comparisons.peer_topic: Cash flow hedge accounting policy and effectiveness assessment
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm designates interest rate derivatives as cash flow hedges for floating-rate assets and uses regression analysis to assess effectiveness. Changes in derivative fair value are recorded in OCI and reclassified to earnings when the hedged item affects earnings, with immediate release if the forecasted cash flow is no longer probable.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS use regression analysis to assess hedge effectiveness. BAC states it uses regression analysis to assess whether derivatives are highly effective in offsetting changes in fair value or cash flows. MS also uses regression analysis for 'ongoing prospective and retrospective assessment of the effectiveness' of its cash flow hedges. Both firms rely on this statistical method for their effectiveness determinations.

sentences.text: The Corporation primarily uses regression analysis at the inception of a hedge and for each reporting period thereafter to assess whether the derivative used in an accounting hedge transaction is expected to be and has been highly effective in offsetting changes in the fair value or cash flows of a hedged item or forecasted transaction.
The Firm uses regression analysis to perform an ongoing prospective and retrospective assessment of the effectiveness of these hedging relationships.
